A changed test exercises the production JSONL transport and observes an old-turn allow become a deny in the subprocess response after reuse. No stored-data contract changes. | | **Evidence reviewed** | 8 items | Current main still needs the repair: The fetched main revision still uses the live-background-task flag and lacks the branch's per-task notification settlement.
Notification settlement: The proposed adapter retains pending task IDs after they leave the live list, consumes queued notification results individually, and ends a turn on a failed result.
Prior finding addressed: The earlier review identified failed notification settlement. The current head consumes a queued task only for a successful result; its changed subprocess tests assert retirement after queued error and malformed-output results. | | **Findings** | None | None. | | **Security** | None | None. | ## How this fits together The Anthropic plugin runs Claude Code as a persistent subprocess for OpenClaw agent turns. It converts CLI task events and permission callbacks into replies and decides when that subprocess can accept another input. ```mermaid flowchart LR A[User turn] --> B[Anthropic CLI backend] B --> C[Claude subprocess] C --> D[Task events and results] D --> E[Pending task tracking] E --> F[Reply delivery] E --> G[Next input] B --> H[Permission decision] H --> C ``` ## Before merge None.

Do we have a high-confidence way to reproduce the issue? Yes. Current-main source and the reported pre-fix Claude trace give a high-confidence path involving an automatically backgrounded foreground Bash task whose completion has no replay receipt; this read-only review did not execute it. Is this the best way to solve the issue? Yes. The existing Anthropic adapter is the narrow owner of the task and result ordering, and the changed transport tests cover queued results, inline receipts, failure retirement, and warm reuse. @clawsweeper re-review

The repaired head is `644a3d02fa1a2b6883fba179d280c56e2a43a489`. Pending work now survives failed notification results, queued completions settle individually, and agent/workflow holds share the same unsettled-task owner. Both overlapping and inline completion probes finished and accepted the next input on the same process. The transport regression also verifies a late prior-turn allow decision becomes a deny in the actual subprocess control response after the next turn starts.

The native three-task probe confirms that two inline replay receipts can share one notification-query result; those receipts do not each promise a later result. No authenticated Anthropic or deployed Gateway proof is claimed.
